samples.summary: None of the design's Goals are reachable on the pinned dependency — the feature ships entirely inert with no way to enable it
samples.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts) requires `@yorkie-js/react >= 0.7.23`; packages/frontend/package.json:66 pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`. Every consumer is behind that gate: `useDurableDocument` refuses eligibility, `PrivateRoute` does not mount `OfflineRuntime`, the Settings switch is hidden (`app/settings/page.tsx` `offlineAvailable &&`), and the chip's offer is suppressed. So no durable client can mount, no store is ever attached, and `saved-locally` is unreachable. The design's Goals — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload or a browser crash" — are therefore delivered for zero users, which the doc itself states in its own § Status ("the Goals below are NOT met by what has shipped") and § Rollout. The Rollout's justification for the dark launch is that the blast radius is "bounded by who turned it on", but nobody can turn it on, so this is not a bounded launch — it is a full subsystem (≈4,000 lines of source plus tests) landing with no user-visible effect, waiting on an upstream release that does not exist yet. Flagging so the panel can weigh whether shipping ahead of the dependency bump is the intended trade; if it is, the finding is answered by the doc rather than by code.

samples.summary: Design doc and README claim the recovery path reuses the document-copy engine; the implementation uses the import engine instead
samples.evidence: Line 613 says "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and line 718's See Also calls document-copy.md "the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The README index entry for this doc repeats it ("Google's conflicted-copy model over the existing copy engine"). The implementation reuses neither: `recoverOfflineCopy` (packages/frontend/src/lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts) calls `createWorkspaceDocument` then `applyImportedContent` — the *import* pipeline from `app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts` — and never touches `copyDocument` (api/documents.ts:109) or `POST /documents/:id/copy`. The code's choice is correct (the copy service copies a server-side source document, and here the source is local archived bytes that the server may no longer have), so this is a stale claim in the canonical doc rather than a wrong implementation — but it misdirects the next reader to the wrong module and the wrong design doc.

samples.summary: Design doc states the 30-day sweep leaves other accounts' archives alone; the implementation deliberately sweeps them across every account
samples.evidence: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:354 — "Archives stay scoped: another account's is the only copy of work their SDK could not reconcile, and it is theirs to collect." packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1232 calls `this.dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` with no user filter, and the comment at :1191 explicitly reverses the doc's reasoning ("Archives are swept on exactly the same terms... scoping the sweep to this user left another account's content with no collection path at all"). `wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts` asserts the unscoped behavior ("collects another account's stale entries and their stale archives"). The code's reasoning is defensible, but the canonical doc now records the opposite rule on a data-retention question — exactly the kind of statement a later reader will implement against.

samples.summary: The README index entry for sync-status.md is now false — it still states offline persistence is deferred and that the chip never claims local durability
samples.evidence: The sync-status.md row in docs/design/README.md is left unchanged and still reads "Offline persistence deferred — `@yorkie-js/sdk@0.7.20` added an opt-in `ClientOptions.store` but we pass none... which is why the wording never claims local durability". This change revises sync-status.md itself (un-marking the Non-Goal, adding the fifth `Saved to this device` state) per the design's PR 5, and adds a new index row for offline-local-persistence.md directly beneath — but the neighbouring summary it contradicts was not updated. The README index is the repo's catalogue of which doc is valid; leaving two adjacent rows asserting opposite things about the same chip is precisely the "file by validity" discipline CONTRIBUTING asks for.

samples.summary: Vestigial option surface: `keepArchives` and `onlyUser` have no caller and their doc comments describe designs the change reversed
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1123) and its pass-through `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` (offline-erase.ts:30) are never called with the option by anything in packages/frontend/src. The comment at :1154 justifies it as being "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired" — but the final design removed that caller entirely (the 401 arm of `fetchWithAuth` now passes `eraseLocalData: "none"` and erases nothing at all). Likewise `dropArchivesWhere(index, range, onlyUser)` at :1351 is only ever called with two arguments, and its comment at :1342 explains that without it "a sweep over `archivedAt` alone would delete another account's on a shared device" — which is exactly the behavior the shipped `collectStale` deliberately performs. Two parameters documented as live guards, both dead, both describing the opposite of what ships. knip checks unused exports, not unused optional parameters, so nothing else catches this.

samples.summary: `deleteWorkspace` pays an unconditional extra `fetchWorkspace` + unfiltered `fetchDocuments()` even where offline persistence can never apply, against the design's "declining the opt-in costs nothing"
samples.evidence: `deleteWorkspace` calls `documentIdsIn(id)` unconditionally before the DELETE, and `documentIdsIn` issues `fetchWorkspace(ref)` plus an unfiltered `fetchDocuments()`. Nothing gates it on `supportsClientKey()`, on the preference, or on `isOfflineUser` — unlike `removeMember` two functions below, which does gate (`const doomed = leaving ? await documentIdsIn(workspaceId) : []`). The design states the promise twice ("Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing"; the `OfflineRuntime` mount note about not paying for an unfiltered `GET /documents` on users who cannot have the feature), and `PrivateRoute` honours it by gating the runtime. On the shipped pin (see the dependency finding) the subsequent `purgeOfflineDocuments` always no-ops because `rememberOfflineUser` is only ever called from the gated `OfflineRuntime`, so the two requests are pure dead work on every workspace deletion. Low user cost — an admin action, two extra reads — but it is the one place the stated invariant is not applied.

samples.summary: Store-key parsing is reimplemented four times despite the store exporting the rule specifically to stop that
samples.evidence: `wafflebase-doc-store.ts:229` exports `documentKeyOf` with the comment "Defined here because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false" — a self-documented prior bug from exactly this duplication. The new code then adds three more private copies: `offline-copy.ts:52` `documentIdOf` (byte-identical to `documentKeyOf`), `offline-erase.ts:390` `documentIdOf` (last segment + strip-to-first-dash), and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:147` `describeArchivedDocument` (last segment + a `TYPE_PREFIXES` table), plus a fourth inline copy of the strip-to-first-dash rule inside `WafflebaseDocStore.storedDocumentIds`. The two prefix rules already disagree in kind — `describeArchivedDocument` refuses `pdf-7` and unprefixed keys, the erase/store pair accept anything — so they are two answers to "which document is this key about" that must be kept in step by hand.

samples.summary: Design doc specifies an `onupgradeneeded` migration the implementation deliberately does not perform
samples.evidence: Line 283: "An `onupgradeneeded` that relocates each existing value into the snapshot store, with an empty change log beside it, is the whole migration." The implementation's `onupgradeneeded` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts) creates the four object stores and explicitly states the opposite: "Version 1 creates; there is nothing in the wild to migrate. No wafflebase build has ever passed `ClientOptions.store`, so no browser holds an older layout." The code's reasoning is right; the doc paragraph describing a relocation step that does not exist should be folded to match.

samples.summary: Unrelated quote-style churn mixed into a feature PR
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts`, `packages/frontend/src/lib/utils.ts` and `packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` are reformatted double-quote-to-single-quote wholesale, well beyond the lines the feature touches (utils.ts's `cn` gains only semicolons). Prettier is write-only here and no lane checks formatting, so this is not CI noise — it is review noise that inflates the diff of an already very large change and makes the substantive edits in those files harder to isolate.

finding.summary: None of the design's Goals are reachable on the pinned dependency — the feature ships entirely inert with no way to enable it
finding.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` (packages/frontend/src/lib/yorkie-capabilities.ts) requires `@yorkie-js/react >= 0.7.23`; packages/frontend/package.json:66 pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`. The Rollout's justification for the dark launch is that the blast radius is "bounded by who turned it on", but nobody can turn it on, so this is not a bounded launch — it is a full subsystem (≈4,000 lines of source plus tests) landing with no user-visible effect, waiting on an upstream release that does not exist yet. verdict.reason: The mechanical facts are accurate — package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22 while yorkie-capabilities.ts:24 requires 0.7.23, so the durable path is inert — but this is not a blocking spec-conformance defect. The canonical design doc itself specifies the inert landing as the intended rollout step, not as an accident: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:45-69 (§ Status, "the Goals below are NOT met by what has shipped… Bumping it is the whole remaining action. No code here changes with it") and :682-692 (§ Rollout, "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release"). The originating work item carries the same accepted outcome (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:40-41 and :242-246, with manual smoke explicitly deferred at :220-221). So the Goals cited belong to the multi-PR feature including the upstream release, not to this change's acceptance criteria. The design-doc discipline requirement of this lens is fully satisfied — one canonical doc under docs/design/, linked at docs/design/README.md:175, documenting the gate rather than a parallel doc. No Non-Goal is crossed, no duplicated logic is introduced, and no existing behavior regresses (PrivateRoute.tsx:25 even keeps the erase/sweep housekeeping alive for a device whose preference outlived a rollback). Crucially, no edit in this repository could remediate it: @yorkie-js/react 0.7.23 depends on yorkie-js-sdk#1357 shipping upstream. That makes this a ship-sequencing judgement already decided and disclosed, whose cost stays inside the codebase (code dead until a one-line bump) — minor under this rubric, and minor never blocks. The reviewer concedes this itself: "if it is [the intended trade], the finding is answered by the doc rather than by code." One evidence detail is also wrong: PrivateRoute.tsx:25 mounts OfflineRuntime when the capability is present OR the preference is already enabled, so it is not unconditionally suppressed.

finding.summary: `OfflineRuntime` is mounted unconditionally, so every signed-in session pays for a feature nobody can enable
finding.evidence: `PrivateRoute` renders `<OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />` with no gate on `supportsClientKey()`, on `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`, or on anything being stored. Its effect (offline-runtime.tsx) unconditionally constructs a `WafflebaseDocStore` (opening/creating the `wafflebase-offline` IndexedDB database), runs `collectStale()`, and awaits `fetchDocuments()` — an extra, un-react-query-cached, unfiltered document listing — before `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`. At the pinned `@yorkie-js/react@0.7.22` nothing can ever be written to that store (`supportsClientKey()` is false), and even after the bump the preference is off by default. The design states the opposite property in § Turning it on: "Users who never opt in pay nothing for this feature existing." The reconcile and sweep are only meaningful once something has been stored, and both the preference and the capability are synchronous checks available at mount, so the early-out is cheap. Cost as shipped: one extra API round trip and one IndexedDB database per session for 100% of users while 0% can benefit.

verdict.reason: The finding states `OfflineRuntime` is mounted "unconditionally … with no gate on `supportsClientKey()`, on `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()`, or on anything being stored." That code is not present. PrivateRoute.tsx:25 computes `const offlineInPlay = supportsClientKey() || getOfflinePersistenceEnabled();` and line 53 renders `{offlineInPlay && <OfflineRuntime userId={String(me.id)} />}` — precisely the two synchronous early-out checks the finding says are missing, with lines 40-52 citing the same design promise ("the design promises that declining the opt-in costs nothing") as the rationale. The finding's quantified cost is also inverted by its own premise: it argues `supportsClientKey()` is false at the pin, and I confirmed the pin is `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (packages/frontend/package.json:66), wired to `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` at vite.config.ts:414-418 and compared against `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"` (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82), while `getOfflinePersistenceEnabled()` defaults to false (offline-persistence-preference.ts:17,40-58). So `offlineInPlay` is false and the component does not mount — the `WafflebaseDocStore` construction, `collectStale()` and `fetchDocuments()` at offline-runtime.tsx:112-178 never run. The claimed "one extra API round trip and one IndexedDB database per session for 100% of users" does not happen for any user at the current pin. The only residual is the `||`: a post-bump capable build mounts the runtime even with the preference off, but that is deliberate and documented (PrivateRoute.tsx:46-49) because the erase-on-disable watcher and owed-erase retry (offline-runtime.tsx:121-134) exist to run when the preference is off, to erase content stored while it was on. That is a different design than the one the finding describes, and it is unreachable at the current pin regardless.

finding.summary: None of the design's Goals are delivered on this branch: the durable path is gated above the pinned dependency
finding.evidence: `supportsClientKey()` compares the injected `__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__` against `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, and `packages/frontend/package.json` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"` (line 66). With the gate closed, `useDurableDocument` refuses every document, no `DurableYorkieProvider` mounts, no store is ever attached, the `saved-locally` chip state is unreachable, and both opt-in entry points (Settings section, chip offer) are hidden. So Goal 1 — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload or a browser crash" — is not satisfied by anything in this diff. The design acknowledges this (§ Rollout: "PR 4 lands inert... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so it is deliberate rather than an oversight, but it means the change ships ~4,000 lines of subsystem whose only integration with a real durable client is exercised by tests that stub `supportsClientKey` to true. Flagging so the tradeoff is weighed explicitly rather than inherited: the reviewable behavior arrives with a later one-line dependency bump that will touch no code here.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim verifies (MinClientKeyVersion "0.7.23" at yorkie-capabilities.ts:24, pin "0.7.22" at packages/frontend/package.json:66, gate applied at use-durable-document.ts:128, collab-document-provider.tsx:223/304, sync-status-chip.tsx:97, settings/page.tsx:35, PrivateRoute.tsx:25), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. The canonical design doc prescribes precisely this shape: docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:659-669 defines PR 4's contents and calls it a bounded dark launch, and lines 682-692 state PR 4 lands inert until the dependency bump. The diff therefore conforms to its spec rather than diverging from it. The tradeoff is also already surfaced in-tree, not inherited: a dedicated Status section at lines 45-69 opens the document with "the Goals below are NOT met by what has shipped", and the task plan repeats it (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:37-41, 220-221, 242-246). Goal 1 cannot be delivered by any code in this repo because it needs @yorkie-js/react 0.7.23 (yorkie-js-sdk#1357), recorded as unreleased (npm latest 0.7.22 as of today), so it is not an acceptance criterion this change could have met. Shipping as-is costs no user anything outside the codebase's own tidiness: no regression, both opt-in surfaces hidden deliberately (lines 252-255), no duplicated logic that will diverge, no stated Non-Goal crossed (lines 85-97). That grades minor/nit ("should have waited for the bump" is an approach preference), and minor/nit never block.

finding.summary: The "dark launch" is not one: on the shipped 0.7.22 pin every document publishes the `unsupported` lapse, so every user's `Not saved` tooltip now blames their browser for our dependency pin
finding.evidence:
`packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `@yorkie-js/react` to `0.7.22`, and `yorkie-capabilities.ts` sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`, so `supportsClientKey()` is false for every render today. The lapse is computed at `collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299` as `decided?.durable ? undefined : !supportsClientKey() ? "unsupported" : …`, and `DurabilityLapseScope` wraps BOTH branches (lines ~340+), i.e. it is published for every collaborative document, durable or not. `sync-status-tooltip.ts` LAPSE_REASONS maps `unsupported` → "This browser cannot save documents locally." and `tooltipFor`'s `not-saved` arm appends it unconditionally (`const why_not = lapse ? ...`).

Net effect on the current pin: 100% of users — nobody has opted in, nobody can — who go offline with unsent edits see a tooltip asserting a false thing about their browser. The design's Rollout section stakes the whole staging argument on "nothing changes for anyone until they opt in" (offline-local-persistence.md § Rollout), and sync-status.md's central risk is "the chip could imply durability it does not have" — this is the mirror of that risk: the chip now mis-attributes the absence of durability. Either gate the lapse scope on the feature being reachable, or give the version-pin case wording that does not accuse the user's browser.

verdict.reason: The finding's mechanism is not present in the code. (1) collab-document-provider.tsx:303-310 computes `const lapse = decided?.durable || !supportsClientKey() ? undefined : !permitted ? "not-permitted" : !offlineEnabled ? "not-enabled" : "another-tab"` — `!supportsClientKey()` yields `undefined`, NOT the claimed `"unsupported"`; the quoted ternary in the finding is misread. (2) There is no `"unsupported"` member in the `DurabilityLapse` union (durable-document-context.ts:104-129), and lines 105-114 document its deliberate omission for exactly the reason the reviewer raises. (3) sync-status-tooltip.ts:35-45 LAPSE_REASONS contains no `unsupported` key and no "This browser cannot save documents locally." string; lines 29-33 record that no lapse is published for a build below MinClientKeyVersion. A repo-wide grep for `unsupported` in packages/frontend/src returns only unrelated matches (`unsupported-type` in offline-copy-recovery.ts:252/276, offline-runtime.tsx:344, test helper names). The pin facts are correct (package.json:66 = "0.7.22"; yorkie-capabilities.ts:24 MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"), so supportsClientKey() is false today — but that is the very branch that publishes no lapse, so `tooltipFor`'s `why_not` (sync-status-tooltip.ts:116) is empty and the tooltip reads exactly as it did before the feature. The claimed user-visible harm cannot occur.
